requirements.evidence: Migrations match the data model (create_totem_presets_table.php:17-23 string(6) nullable unique login_code, json appearance; totem_preset_queue composite PK at :25). Command: random_int + str_pad (PairingCodeCommand.php:50), 10 min expiry, clears consumed_at (:58-62), audit log (:64), FAILURE on unknown preset (:43-47). Auth: 400 invalid_code_format via /^\d{6}$/D (TotemAuthController.php:184-188), identical 401 for unknown/expired/consumed/inactive (:196-218, :262-264), lockForUpdate inside DB::transaction (:190-194), totem created active with last_seen_at (:230-235), entity slug/name in response (:255-258). JWT HS256 with iat/exp/jti (TotemJwt.php:819-823), config keys in config/services.php:57-61, .env.example:9-13, phpunit.xml:1802-1803. Middleware checks every 401 case and intersects claim with current join (AuthenticateTotem.php:509-540). Endpoints: 403 entity mismatch, 404 queue_not_found scoped to entity, 403 out-of-scope (TotemQueueController.php:437-453), ordered active queues with 1-based order (:323-330), priorities 0/10/20 from one enum (TicketPriority.php), ticket via IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (:395) and 201 payload. Throttles 10/min and 30/min (routes/api.php), 429 rate_limited render (bootstrap/app.php:1032-1046), strict CORS (TotemCors.php:631-637). Docs updated (docs/api/totem.md, architecture.md, database-schema.md).

conventions.evidence: Domain write goes through App\Actions\IssueTicket (TotemQueueController.php:395); models use #[Fillable] like sibling Queue.php; migrations have reversible down(); required docs are synced. Deviations: CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] not updated, although conventions require it; migration names with sequential 000000/000001/000002 timestamps suggest they were written by hand rather than generated with make:migration; request input (code, priority) is checked by hand instead of $request->validate()/Form Request (needed for the custom error codes, but it departs from the stated pattern).

security.evidence: Constant-time signature check with hash_equals and alg pinned to HS256 (TotemJwt.php:848-856); exp required (:864); empty secret refused (:895-897). Middleware rejects inactive/mismatched totem, preset and entity (AuthenticateTotem.php:518-528) and narrows scope to the current join (:540). Queue lookup is scoped by entity_id before the scope check, so no cross-entity leak (TotemQueueController.php:439-450). Pairing has no oracle (single 401), is throttled and audited without logging the code (TotemAuthController.php:279-287). CORS allow-list uses an anchored regex and no credentials (TotemCors.php:631). Mass assignment: forceFill is used only for server-set fields. No weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Totem/TotemApiTest.php covers format errors (:1865-1876), happy pairing incl. claims and consumption (:1878-1906), all four 401 pairing states (:1908-1930), 429 throttle (:1932-1942), six invalid-token cases (:1944-1984), ordering/scope/intersection (:1986-2029), priorities and inactive queue (:2031-2060), sequential A001/A002 with channel totem (:2062-2086), invalid priorities create nothing (:2088-2101), cross-entity 404/403 (:2118-2133), CORS preflight and disallowed origin (:2135-2150), command success/failure, attach/detach. Missing: a ticket POST into a queue that exists but is outside scope (403), the 30/min issuance throttle, the TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN allow path, and audit-log assertions.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean: the enum is the single priority source, IssueTicket is reused, and the JWT is a small HS256 class (allowed by the task). Some extra machinery: TotemPresentation reads per-queue appearance overrides (TotemPresentation.php:958-971), which the task did not ask for; the integer-parsing helpers are duplicated (TicketPriority::fromRequest vs AuthenticateTotem::integerClaim); CORS headers are applied twice on exception responses (global middleware plus the exceptions->respond hook at bootstrap/app.php:1024-1030).

readability.evidence: Clear names and small private helpers (resolveQueue, forbidden, auditFailure); PHPDoc explains intent (AuthenticateTotem.php:479-485, TotemCors.php:584-590). Minor oddities: the nullsafe Log::channel('audit')?-> is used where channel() never returns null (PairingCodeCommand.php:64, TotemAuthController.php:271); the positional tuple from context() with skipped slots ([$tokenEntity, , $queueIds]) is slightly opaque.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Small extras: an inverse Queue::totemPresets() relation (app/Models/Queue.php:681-685) that is not required, per-queue appearance overrides in TotemPresentation, and an unrequested rewrite of prose in docs/api/totem.md (e.g. removed the 'Steps' section, :1381-1399).

issues.explanation: The conventions require a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased], but the change adds a new public API, a new command and new tables without one.
The sequential 000000/000001/000002 timestamps suggest hand-written migrations, which the conventions forbid (they require php artisan make:migration).
No test for a ticket POST to an in-entity but out-of-scope queue (403), the 30/min issuance throttle, the TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN allowed origin, or the audit log entries.
Per-queue appearance overrides (description/color/icon from totem_presets.appearance) are speculative; the task only needs the visual fields to be present.
Exception responses get CORS headers from both the global TotemCors middleware and the respond hook, so the work is done twice and Vary: Origin can be appended twice.
Log::channel('audit')?-> uses a nullsafe operator on a call that never returns null, which misleads readers.
The inverse Queue::totemPresets() relation is not required by the contract and is unused.

review.summary: The change implements totem pairing (artisan command, POST /api/totem/auth with a locked transaction and an in-repo HS256 JWT), the totem.auth middleware with scope intersection, the three entity/queue endpoints that reuse IssueTicket with channel totem, throttling, strict CORS and the doc updates. It meets essentially every requirement and has broad, meaningful tests. The remaining points are minor: CHANGELOG is not updated, migrations look hand-written, a few tests are missing (out-of-scope ticket POST, issuance throttle) and the appearance-override presentation goes beyond the task, so I would approve with nits.
